messages:
Jen-Customer: hitting 403s on our app when calling /v1/completions. It used to work. We didn’t change keys. Response body is just "Forbidden". Help?

Sophie: sorry about this — can you paste the exact curl (or SDK call) and the full response body? also which account/org id?

Jen-Customer: minimal repro:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXX" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/completions -d '{"model":"rwd-sm-1","prompt":"hi"}'

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "Forbidden"
}

org: org_92b

Sophie: thanks. grabbing logs (req id would help if present). I'll check entitlement and auth traces.

entitlement-bot: [auto] req=req_0e4a org=org_92b outcome=blocked check=plan_lookup feature_flag=quota_enforcement_v2 detail=plan_missing

Sophie: hmm entitlement check failed (plan missing) and returned a generic 403 body. That explains the confusing auth message. tagging @Alex for runtime change — we should return an entitlement-specific error code and message.

Alex: saw the bot trace. We shipped quota_enforcement_v2 to prod yesterday as a gated flag; if plan metadata is null we treat as blocked and return 403 w/ empty body (legacy path). We need two things: 1) change error JSON to include "entitlement" reason, 2) add extra logging (plan_id/null) and telemetry so support can quickly diagnose. I can put up a small patch.

Mike: billing checked — org_92b is from a migration batch; they didn't accept new billing terms so plan row is null. From billing side we can populate a default entry but it might be safer to have runtime return clearer error first.

Sophie: agree. action plan:
- Alex: patch runtime to return 403 with body like `{
  "error": "entitlement_denied",
  "entitlement_reason": "plan_missing",
  "reference": "REQ_ID"
}` and add metric tag `entitlement_reason`. PR and canary today.
- Billing (Mike): follow up with Jen on plan acceptance flow.
- Support (Sophie): add repro steps and note for docs/FAQ.

Alex: putting up PR #4127 — small change in middleware. will add unit + add a debug header `X-RW-Plan-Status: missing` in canary so support can read it from curl. pushing to canary in ~30m.

entitlement-bot: [auto] deploy-trigger pr=4127 env=canary status=started

Jen-Customer: thanks. will watch. can you confirm this is not a key/scope issue? we had different teams worried about token scopes.

Sophie: confirmed — keys are fine. this is plan/entitlement gating surfaced incorrectly as a plain 403. after Alex's change the response will be explicit and SDKs will map to EntitlementError (not AuthError).

Alex: canary is up. sample curl now returns:

HTTP/1.1 403 Forbidden
{
  "error": "entitlement_denied",
  "entitlement_reason": "plan_missing",
  "reference": "req_0e4a"
}

Sophie: Jen — can you retry and paste the body if still failing?

Jen-Customer: retried — now I see entitlement_denied and reference req_0e4a. thx. We'll get billing to accept and then confirm.

Mike: Billing will update org_92b today. will CC Sophie when done.

Sophie: leaving a short internal note for docs + support runbook: include checklist: 
- check response body for `entitlement_` keys
- check `X-RW-Plan-Status` header in canary logs (will be removed after rollout)
- if plan missing, route to billing ops.

Alex: opened follow-up ticket RW-9876 to remove the canary header post rollout and to add a more specific HTTP status mapping in SDKs.

Sophie: marking this resolved for now, but keeping thread open until billing confirms and Jen verifies production traffic. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

Jen-Customer: confirmed after billing update — all good in prod. thanks team! :rocket:
